chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Identifying the Navy band photograph
summary: Royal names members in a photo of the St. Mary's Pre-Flight band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: ~~ (Inaudible) ~~ The other thing I wanted to ask you. I found this picture from a magazine -- I don't know what the magazine was, but it's ~~ a ~~ in Jerome Richardson's scrapbook and it's a picture of your Navy band and I wonder if you

I can tell you the name of most of them right offhand. Starting from the left, piano player is Wilbur Branoo (PHONETIC). He's a teacher up at the University of California now. Standing next to him is Vernon Alley, excellent bassist and a stalwart San Franciscan. Then the guitar player is Benny -- I can't think of his last name. He has since passed. Tenor saxophone player in the front there is Andy Anderson out of Cleveland, Ohio. Next to him is Q. Dellis Martin (PHONETIC), who is now living in Honolulu. Next to him is Jackie Kellson (PHONETIC), Hollywood studio musician. Next to him is Jerome Richardson, saxophone, Hollywood studio musician. Next to him is --
The leader is standing there, right?

No, there's another fellow that is not seen. I'll recall his name in a minute. Then the trombone player in the middle is Ralph Bledsoe (PHONETIC) who at the present time is one of our better known physicians in town. He's a urologist. He's flanked on both sides by two trombone players, both of them -- one of them, his name is Dan Hamilton. The drummer is San Franciscan. He's a business agent for the San Francisco local and his name is Earl Watkins. The first trumpet player there next to him is my kid brother, Ernie Royal. The next trumpet player is a fellow from Chico, California. His name is -- his last name is Saunders. Next to him is one of the
old Kansas City trumpet players, Herman Grimes. The other trumpet player is one of a set of twins, the Gregory twins. I'm on the end over there somewhere.
I see you there, with your clarinet in your hand.
That's great. You got everybody, I think, but one.

Yeah, I'll think of his name in a minute. I should think of it better because my brother and he married two sisters. Curtis Lowe (PHONETIC) is the baritone saxophone player. He's now the recording secretary with Local 6, San Francisco Musician's Union.
Thank you very much. Glad to have that. (Inaudible)
